# PixelLab pixel work — HIGH thinking mode

Think openly. Before each call, write your plan in a few short sentences; after
each result, say what you actually see — what worked and what is wrong — before
you decide the next step. Put the same reasoning in the tool's `notes` (it is
stored with the step). Pass `mode="high"`: results then carry fuller evidence
(every frame, body-only vs effects, palette, before/after with change masks).

Every exact call below is one tool, `pixelart_workbench(argv=[…])`; `argv` is a
list, so a JSON payload rides as its own item.

## Pick the tool

| The user wants | Call |
| --- | --- |
| Exact change: recolour, outline, fix specific pixels, copy a detail between frames, clean flicker/drift frame by frame | `edit <id> --changes '[…]'` (free, exact, no AI) |
| Exact colours and coordinates | `inspect <id>`; `--region x0,y0,x1,y1` gives a zoomed crop and a pixel grid |
| Animate a still sprite you design (wave, bob, blink, attack, cast) or draw art from shapes | `draw --recipe '{…}'` — read `describe draw` and `describe animation` first |
| A new image or character | `create_image_pixen` (cheap) · `create_image_pro` (best, returns candidates) · `create_character` |
| An AI edit by instruction / regenerate one region | `edit_image_pixen` · `edit_image` · `inpaint_image` |
| AI animation from a description | `animate_character` · `animate_image` |
| Clean generated art automatically | `correct_pixelart` · `reduce_colors` (all frames in one call) · `unzoom_image` |
| A sprite sheet, strip or grid as frames (to play it, check it or edit it as an animation) | `split <id> --grid 8x1` — columns x rows (free) |
| Pictures or animations put together: one sprite sheet, one animation per row, or one longer animation | `join <id> <id> … [--as sheet\|rows\|animation] [--columns n]` (free; smaller pictures are padded, never rescaled) |
| The same picture or animation bigger (a sticker, a print, a banner) | `scale <id> --by 4` — each pixel a 4x4 block, whole numbers only, up to 1024 px a side (free; nothing is redrawn: redrawn at a bigger size, art loses its details) |
| Keep the fix in the user's character, object or Creator gallery image (creators, gallery, downloads, game projects) | `save_to_asset(image="<id>", target="character:<id>:<direction>[:<group id>]")`, or `object:<id>[:<direction>][:<group id>]`, or `gallery:<id>` — same canvas and frame count, one call per direction; the reply has an undo. `gallery:new` adds it to the gallery as a new image (any size; give it a `description`) |

The strongest results combine them: generate or animate with the AI tools, then
review every frame and repair exactly with `edit`, or build precise motion
and effects yourself with `draw`.

## Images

`image` accepts `character:<id>:<direction>`, `character:<id>:<direction>:<animation>`,
`object:<id>[:<direction>[:<animation>]]`, `gallery:<id>` (a Creator gallery
image — `list_images` finds them), `job:<id>[:<index>]` (an image tool's result), any
pixel tool id (`<id>:<view>` for a drawing view), or a URL. Every result is a
new id; pass ids, never pixels.

## Protocol

1. **Goal.** Restate the request. List what must survive: identity, palette and
   material ramps, outline colour and thickness, timing, intended motion and
   effects. Include the user's words in the first call's `notes`.
2. **Look.** `inspect` every input frame. Record canvas, frame count,
   durations, palette, outline colour, defects. New colours and one-frame
   elements are things to inspect, not automatically errors.
3. **Plan.** Choose the tool. For animation: phases (anticipation → action →
   recovery), which parts move and around which pivot, what surfaces a moving
   part will reveal, how much canvas the motion needs.
4. **Act.** One call with related changes batched; every operation's `reason`
   names the observation it fixes.
5. **Review — the evidence gates:**

   | After | Check |
   | --- | --- |
   | first render / first look | every frame: silhouette, contact points, parts carried or detached, revealed gaps |
   | each edit | before/after/changes: only the intended pixels changed? neighbours intact? |
   | a suspected flicker or wandering pixel | that frame and its neighbours, zoomed 8–10x |
   | a possibly damaged motion or effect | the whole phase: onset, peak, disappearance |
   | before finishing | all final frames, the loop seam, outline continuity, stray clusters at 8–10x |

6. **Decide:** inspect (a detail is uncertain), edit (an observed defect), or
   finish. If two passes bring no improvement, keep the best result and say
   what remains instead of forcing it.
7. **Finish.** Tell the user what changed, what you verified, what is left, and
   give the download links. When the input was their character, object or
   gallery image, offer to `save_to_asset` the result back (and keep the undo it
   returns).

## Craft rules (from tested runs)

- Never rescale pixel art; give motion and outlines canvas room instead.
- Keep the source palette and outline style; add colours only for new materials
  or effects, as a proper ramp.
- Moving cut-out parts reveal hidden surfaces (a torso behind an arm, a
  shoulder) — draw them, then check at 10x.
- Thin parts (a 2–3 px limb) rotate into broken slivers; redraw the pose with
  shapes/pixels instead of rotating the cut-out.
- Use integer positions (step keys) for moving parts; half pixels jitter.
- Fewer colours or a lower flicker count is not proof of a better image, and a
  GIF link is not proof you watched the animation — judge the frames you saw.
- Guarded patches: read the exact colour on that layer first (layer inspection),
  it can differ from the flattened image.


---
Other topics: draw, animation, motion, scenes, edits, paint, outline, review

review before your next call: say what you see in the images — what worked, what is wrong (outline gaps, stray or carried pixels, colours off the palette, parts detached at joints, flicker between neighbouring frames) — then choose: inspect (uncertain), edit (observed defect), or finish. Put that reasoning in `notes`.
